blueprint_topic: Safety and Infection Prevention and Control — prospective elopement-risk prevention using observation, environmental, and access controls matched to assessed risk
stem: An inpatient psychiatric client repeatedly asks about exit locations and how visitor badges open doors. Which nursing action best addresses the identified elopement risk?

options.A: Continue routine observation and document the questions, because preventive elopement precautions are unnecessary until the client makes an actual exit attempt.
options.B: Use the unit's elopement-risk process now, adding observation and environmental or access controls that match the assessed risk rather than waiting for an attempt.
options.C: Move the client closer to the nurses' station and keep the usual observation level, because location alone is sufficient once staff can see the hallway more easily.
options.D: Ask family to reinforce staying on the unit and defer environmental precautions, because discussing exit locations does not justify a prevention plan without prior elopement.

rationale: B is correct. AHRQ PSNet describes elopement prevention as a system-based process that begins with risk assessment and special preventive precautions for at-risk patients rather than waiting for an actual elopement. Preventive measures may include enhanced or constant observation, placement strategies, electronic monitoring, alarms, automatic door locks, and other environmental/access controls appropriate to the patient's risk and the care setting. Joint Commission guidance also recognizes specialized security measures and door-locking arrangements in psychiatric and other settings when clinical needs justify elopement prevention, subject to life-safety requirements. A is incorrect because prevention should begin when risk is identified, not only after an exit attempt. C is incomplete because proximity to the nurses' station can be one precaution but does not replace a risk-based plan. D is incorrect because family reinforcement may support care but does not substitute for organizational precautions when behavior indicates elopement risk.
educational_objective: Respond to identified elopement risk prospectively by activating the organization's risk-based prevention process and using observation plus environmental or access controls appropriate to the assessed risk.
source_organization: Agency for Healthcare Research and Quality (AHRQ) PSNet; The Joint Commission; National Council of State Boards of Nursing (NCSBN)
source_document_title: Elopement; Means of Egress — Locking Doors; 2026 NCLEX-RN Test Plan
source_version_date: AHRQ PSNet elopement commentary and current indexed elopement evidence rechecked 2026-08-21; Joint Commission egress/security guidance current when rechecked 2026-08-21; 2026 NCLEX-RN Test Plan effective April 2026
source_locator: AHRQ PSNet Elopement: patients should be assessed for elopement risk throughout hospitalization; at-risk patients should receive special preventive precautions. The commentary lists observation protocols, closer placement, electronic monitoring, automatic door locks, alarms, and other measures as examples matched to setting/risk. AHRQ PSNet 2024 indexed evidence describes an organizational elopement-management plan using risk evaluation plus response algorithms. Joint Commission Means of Egress guidance recognizes specialized security/door-locking arrangements for psychiatric and other units when patient clinical needs justify elopement prevention, subject to life-safety criteria. NCSBN 2026 NCLEX-RN Test Plan Safety and Infection Prevention and Control detailed content includes security plans/procedures and environmental injury prevention.
source_claim_supported: Fresh current evidence supports prospective risk assessment and special preventive precautions for elopement risk, with observation and environmental/access controls chosen according to patient and setting. The item does not prescribe a universal 1:1 interval or a single security device.

pdf_visual_verification: PASS — relevant official 2026 NCLEX-RN Test Plan Safety and Infection Prevention and Control pages were freshly screenshot-verified earlier in this continuation. AHRQ and Joint Commission evidence used for Q0316 is current HTML; no new PDF evidence is relied on.
correction_summary: Original Q0316 had a uniquely longest correct answer. The item was rebuilt with four realistic responses of similar length. The key now emphasizes timely activation of a risk-based elopement-prevention process while avoiding an unsupported universal observation frequency or mandatory device.

option_audit.A: Plausible documentation-first approach; incorrect because preventive precautions should begin when risk is identified rather than after an actual attempt.
option_audit.B: Correct; directly reflects risk assessment plus observation and environmental/access controls matched to risk.
option_audit.C: Plausible location-based precaution; incorrect because closer placement alone does not replace a comprehensive risk-based prevention plan.
option_audit.D: Plausible family-support measure; incorrect because family reinforcement does not substitute for organizational precautions when risk behavior is present.

cueing_audit.absolute_words: No option relies on all/only/always/never wording as its sole cue.
cueing_audit.answer_length: Final option lengths: A 160, B 163, C 164, D 174 characters; the key is not longest and there is no positive length cue.
cueing_audit.grammatical_lexical: All four alternatives are realistic preventive strategies and differ in timing and breadth of the response rather than obvious wording quality.
cueing_audit.second_answer_risk: No defensible second answer identified in the pre-stage audit. C contains one valid precaution but explicitly treats it as sufficient; A and D defer needed prevention. Post-fetch adversarial reread remains required.
